derive signer assurance and distinct-person identity from admitted descriptors; legacy AdminKey person/strength are not proof

bind canonical versioned bytes to action pool anchor target signer context nonce expiry authority generation and result IDs
revalidate current authority operation and runtime handles immediately before signature and consumption
persist roots observed heads complete-first-sight awake times distrust fatigue and consumption outside node rollback domain; missing checkpoint refuses; no auto-repin

privileged effects use durable prepare consume effect reconcile receipts; unknown outcome is recovery_required; committed or signed never implies performed

unresolved_gaps: Platform protected presentation, fresh presence, actual endpoint authentication and root admission producers remain unimplemented and unproved.
Shared root/checkpoint storage must survive independent node rollback and reinstall; OS mechanism and atomic receipt protocol await platform review.
Closed grant actions are deliberately bounded; retained grant actions outside this subset require explicit typed scope review before retention can be claimed.
Founding/admit descriptor references require authenticated independent verification; references alone are untrusted. Node supplies transport identity and removal cuts.
Cryptographic encoding negotiation for retained P-256 keys and signatures needs a typed variant; ApprovalSignature64 alone does not replace P-256.
Handoff/reissue and shared-board charter authority require their own complete typed domains before they can be requested; no in-place join-policy change.
GovernanceMode members remains explicitly unsupported until its authority implementation is reviewed; join policy is a separate immutable field.
Legacy person enrollment, raw draft signing, approval_decide, typed confirmation, and requests.approved booleans confer no new authority and have no migration path.
Independent review and generator integration/drift checks remain required; source mapping is not complete feature retention or installed acceptance.

Legacy grants to other sessions, classes or accounts are outside the own-requester-only grant subset; mapping grant_issue records the family, not complete retention. They require separate reviewed recipient contracts before retention can be claimed.
